turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hi, mister. Washington, come on back. Before we get going, can you confirm your full name and date of birth for me?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: February 9,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Perfect thank you. How was the drive -in? I heard the parking garage was full again this morning.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Sorry about that, so this is your blood pressure follow -up.

turns.text: How have things been since we saw you in July? pretty good mostly I've been checking it at home like you said and it's still kind of high usually like 145 150 on the top number okay that's helpful and what are you taking for it right now the listen April 10 milligrams in the morning wait no it's 20 you bumped it up last time remember I've got the new bottle in the car.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good trick and you're still on the adorvastatin for your cholesterol.

turns.text: Great,

turns.text: any headaches,

turns.text: chest pain or trouble catching your breath?

turns.text: Any cough since you've been on the listen, April. Some people get a dry, tickly cough with it.

turns.text: And alcohols.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A couple beers on the weekend, that's about it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, and you mentioned your dad before, right?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, my father had a stroke at 62. That's kind of why my wife Lorraine stays on me about all this.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That makes sense. She's looking out for you. All right, your blood pressure today is 152 over 94. And when I rechecked it after you sat quietly for five minutes, it was 148 over 92. Pulse is 72. Weight is 214 pounds. That's up three pounds from July.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, that's the Halloween candy starting early,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I guess. Let me take a listen, heart sounds regular no murmurs, lungs are clear and no swelling in your legs. I also have your labs from last week. Your potassium was 4 .4 and your kidney function was normal, create a 9 .0 .9. And your LDL cholesterol was 88.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Is that good?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: The cholesterol is right where we want it. And the kidneys and potassium look fine, which means we have room to go up on the listen -april.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So here's what I'm thinking. Your blood pressure is still above our goal of under 130 over 80, even on the 20 milligrams. I'd like to increase the listen -up to 40 milligrams once a day. Until you run out, you can take two of your 20s together in the morning.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Two of the 20s, got it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Keep the adorv acid in the same 40 milligrams at night. I'd also like you to cut back on salt, aim for less than 2 ,000 milligrams a day. The deli meat and chips are big ones.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I can try packing lunch, Lorraine will be thrilled.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That would help a lot. Since we're raising the dose, I want to repeat potassium and kidney check in about two weeks. You can go to our lab on Brookfield Avenue, no appointment needed.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm off on the 19th, does that work?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: The 19th is perfect. Keep checking at home and bring your log next time. If you get readings over 180 on the top, or a severe headache, chest pain or weakness on one side, call us or go to the emergency room.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: We'll do.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: And I'll see you back in six weeks. Is your cell still 555 -0163?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yep, same number.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Great any other questions for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, I think that's it. Thanks, Dark.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Take care, Darnell. Good luck with the parking on the way out. out.
